Salon Cost Calculator

Get a rough, informational estimate of what a salon visit might cost based on your hair length and the services you're considering.

Services

Estimated Salon Cost

This calculator provides an estimated price range for informational purposes only. Actual salon prices vary by location, stylist, service complexity, hair length, products and salon. These figures are not official Sola Salon Studios prices.

How This Estimate Works

The calculator combines a base price per service with adjustments for hair length, salon tier and stylist experience to produce a plausible range — not an exact quote. Always confirm final pricing with your stylist before booking.

Why Salon Prices Vary So Much

It's common to see the same service — a haircut, a set of highlights — priced anywhere from $30 to $300 depending on where you look, and that range isn't arbitrary. In the salon-studio model in particular, every independent professional sets their own rates based on their training, years of experience, the cost of the products they use, and how much demand they have for their time. A newer stylist building a client base will typically charge less than someone with a decade of experience and a long waitlist, even for an identical service. Location also plays a real role — rent and cost of living in a given city or neighborhood factor into what a professional needs to charge to sustain their business.

What the Inputs Actually Adjust

Hair length affects cost because longer hair simply takes more product and more time to process, cut, or color evenly — a full head of foils on waist-length hair uses substantially more product than the same service on a chin-length bob. Salon tier reflects the general pricing bracket a business operates in, from budget-friendly to premium. Stylist experience captures the reality that more experienced professionals, particularly those who specialize in a specific technique like color correction or curly cutting, generally charge a premium for that expertise.

Getting the Most Accurate Estimate

For the most useful estimate, select every service you're actually considering in the same visit rather than calculating them one at a time — many salons offer a small discount for bundled services, so a combined estimate here is closer to what a real multi-service quote might look like, even though it doesn't account for that specific discount. If you're planning a significant change, like going from dark to very light hair, keep in mind that a responsible stylist may recommend spreading the service across two or more appointments, which would roughly double the total cost compared to what a single-visit estimate here suggests.

Using This Before You Call

Think of this tool as a way to set expectations before you reach out to a stylist, not as a substitute for an actual quote. Most professionals are happy to give a more precise price once they know your hair's current condition and exact goal — this calculator just helps you walk into that conversation with a realistic budget range already in mind.
